HACCP_term.description: Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP) guide food safety term. Hazard Analysis Critical Control Points (HACCP) food safety terms; This field accepts terms listed under HACCP guide food safety term (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03530221). Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

IFSAC_category.description: Interagency Food Safety Analytics Collaboration (IFSAC) category. The IFSAC food categorization scheme has five distinct levels to which foods can be assigned, depending upon the type of food. First, foods are assigned to one of four food groups (aquatic animals, land animals, plants, and other). Food groups include increasingly specific food categories; dairy, eggs, meat and poultry, and game are in the land animal food group, and the category meat and poultry is further subdivided into more specific categories of meat (beef, pork, other meat) and poultry (chicken, turkey, other poultry). Finally, foods are differentiated by differences in food processing (such as pasteurized fluid dairy products, unpasteurized fluid dairy products, pasteurized solid and semi-solid dairy products, and unpasteurized solid and semi-solid dairy products. An IFSAC food category chart is available from https://www.cdc.gov/foodsafety/ifsac/projects/food-categorization-scheme.html PMID: 28926300

abs_air_humidity.description: absolute air humidity. Actual mass of water vapor present in the air water vapor mixture.. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

adapters.description: adapters. Adapters provide priming sequences for both amplification and sequencing of the sample-library fragments. Both adapters should be reported; in uppercase letters. Syntax: ^{dna_bases};{dna_bases}$

add_recov_method.description: secondary and tertiary recovery methods and start date. Additional (i.e. Secondary, tertiary, etc.) recovery methods deployed for increase of hydrocarbon recovery from resource and start date for each one of them. If "other" is specified, please propose entry in "additional info" field. Syntax: ^({add_recov_methods});{date_time_stamp}$

additional_info.description: additional info. Information that doesn't fit anywhere else. Can also be used to propose new entries for fields with controlled vocabulary

address.description: address. The street name and building number where the sampling occurred. Syntax: ^{integer} {text}$

adj_room.description: adjacent rooms. List of rooms (room number, room name) immediately adjacent to the sampling room. Syntax: ^{room_name};{room_number}$

adjacent_environment.description: environment adjacent to site. Description of the environmental system or features that are adjacent to the sampling site. This field accepts terms under ecosystem (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_01001110) and human construction (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000070). Multiple terms can be separated by pipes

aero_struc.description: aerospace structure. Aerospace structures typically consist of thin plates with stiffeners for the external surfaces, bulkheads and frames to support the shape and fasteners such as welds, rivets, screws and bolts to hold the components together

agrochem_addition.description: history/agrochemical additions. Addition of fertilizers, pesticides, etc. - amount and time of applications. Syntax: ^{agrochemical_name};{amount} {unit};{date_time_stamp}$

air_PM_concen.description: air particulate matter concentration. Concentration of substances that remain suspended in the air, and comprise mixtures of organic and inorganic substances (PM10 and PM2.5); can report multiple PM's by entering numeric values preceded by name of PM. Syntax: ^{particulate_matter_name};{float} {unit}$

air_flow_impede.description: local air flow impediments. Presence of objects in the area that would influence or impede air flow through the air filter

air_temp.description: air temperature. Temperature of the air at the time of sampling. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

air_temp_regm.description: air temperature regimen. Information about treatment involving an exposure to varying temperatures; should include the temperature, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include different temperature regimens

al_sat.description: extreme_unusual_properties/Al saturation. Aluminum saturation (esp. For tropical soils). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

al_sat_meth.description: extreme_unusual_properties/Al saturation method. Reference or method used in determining Al saturation. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

alkalinity.description: alkalinity. Alkalinity, the ability of a solution to neutralize acids to the equivalence point of carbonate or bicarbonate. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

alkalinity_method.description: alkalinity method. Method used for alkalinity measurement

alkyl_diethers.description: alkyl diethers. Concentration of alkyl diethers. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

alt.description: altitude. Heights of objects such as airplanes, space shuttles, rockets, atmospheric balloons and heights of places such as atmospheric layers and clouds. It is used to measure the height of an object which is above the earth's surface. In this context, the altitude measurement is the vertical distance between the earth's surface above sea level and the sampled position in the air. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

aminopept_act.description: aminopeptidase activity. Measurement of aminopeptidase activity. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ammonium.description: ammonium. Concentration of ammonium in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

amniotic_fluid_color.description: amniotic fluid/color. Specification of the color of the amniotic fluid sample

amount_light.description: amount of light. The unit of illuminance and luminous emittance, measuring luminous flux per unit area. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ances_data.description: ancestral data. Information about either pedigree or other ancestral information description (e.g. parental variety in case of mutant or selection), e.g. A/3*B (meaning [(A x B) x B] x B)

anim_water_method.description: animal water delivery method. Description of the equipment or method used to distribute water to livestock. This field accepts termed listed under water delivery equipment (http://opendata.inra.fr/EOL/EOL_0001653). Multiple terms can be separated by pipes. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

animal_am.description: food animal antimicrobial. The name(s) (generic or brand) of the antimicrobial(s) given to the food animal within the last 30 days

animal_am_dur.description: food animal antimicrobial duration. The duration of time (days) that the antimicrobial was administered to the food animal. Syntax: ^{float} days$

animal_am_freq.description: food animal antimicrobial frequency. The frequency per day that the antimicrobial was administered to the food animal. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

animal_am_route.description: food animal antimicrobial route of administration. The route by which the antimicrobial is administered into the body of the food animal

animal_am_use.description: food animal antimicrobial intended use. The prescribed intended use of or the condition treated by the antimicrobial given to the food animal by any route of administration

animal_body_cond.description: food animal body condition. Body condition scoring is a production management tool used to evaluate overall health and nutritional needs of a food animal. Because there are different scoring systems, this field is restricted to three categories

animal_diet.description: food animal source diet. If the isolate is from a food animal, the type of diet eaten by the food animal.  Please list the main food staple and the setting, if appropriate.  For a list of acceptable animal feed terms or categories, please see http://www.feedipedia.org.  Multiple terms may apply and can be separated by pipes |Food product for animal covers foods intended for consumption by domesticated animals. Consult http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03309997. If the proper descriptor is not listed please use text to describe the food type. Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes. If the proper descriptor is not listed please use text to describe the food product type

animal_feed_equip.description: animal feeding equipment. Description of the feeding equipment used for livestock. This field accepts terms listed under feed delivery (http://opendata.inra.fr/EOL/EOL_0001757). Multiple terms can be separated by pipes. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

animal_group_size.description: food animal group size. The number of food animals of the same species that are maintained together as a unit, i.e. a herd or flock

animal_housing.description: animal housing system. Description of the housing system of the livestock. This field accepts terms listed under terrestrial management housing system (http://opendata.inra.fr/EOL/EOL_0001605). Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

animal_intrusion.description: animal intrusion near sample source. Identification of animals intruding on the sample or sample site including invertebrates (such as pests or pollinators) and vertebrates (such as wildlife or domesticated animals). This field accepts terms under organism (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCIT_C14250). This field also accepts identification numbers from NCBI under https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy. Multiple terms can be separated by pipes. Syntax: ^(({termLabel} \[{termID}\])|{integer})$

animal_sex.description: food animal source sex category. The sex and reproductive status of the food animal

annot.description: annotation. Tool used for annotation, or for cases where annotation was provided by a community jamboree or model organism database rather than by a specific submitter

annual_precpt.description: mean annual precipitation. The average of all annual precipitation values known, or an estimated equivalent value derived by such methods as regional indexes or Isohyetal maps. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

annual_temp.description: mean annual temperature. Mean annual temperature. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

antibiotic_regm.description: antibiotic regimen. Information about treatment involving antibiotic administration; should include the name of antibiotic, amount administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple antibiotic regimens

api.description: API gravity. API gravity is a measure of how heavy or light a petroleum liquid is compared to water (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API_gravity) (e.g. 31.1   API). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

arch_struc.description: architectural structure. An architectural structure is a human-made, free-standing, immobile outdoor construction

area_samp_size.description: area sampled size. The total amount or size (volume (ml), mass (g) or area (m2) ) of sample collected

aromatics_pc.description: aromatics wt%. Saturate, Aromatic, Resin and Asphaltene (SARA) is an analysis method that divides crude oil components according to their polarizability and polarity. There are three main methods to obtain SARA results. The most popular one is known as the Iatroscan TLC-FID and is referred to as IP-143 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturate,_aromatic,_resin_and_asphaltene). Syntax: ^{name};{float} {unit}$

asphaltenes_pc.description: asphaltenes wt%. Saturate, Aromatic, Resin and Asphaltene (SARA) is an analysis method that divides crude oil components according to their polarizability and polarity. There are three main methods to obtain SARA results. The most popular one is known as the Iatroscan TLC-FID and is referred to as IP-143 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturate,_aromatic,_resin_and_asphaltene). Syntax: ^{name};{float} {unit}$

assembly_name.description: assembly name. Name/version of the assembly provided by the submitter that is used in the genome browsers and in the community

assembly_qual.description: assembly quality. The assembly quality category is based on sets of criteria outlined for each assembly quality category. For MISAG/MIMAG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities with a consensus error rate equivalent to Q50 or better. High Quality Draft:Multiple fragments where gaps span repetitive regions. Presence of the large subunit (LSU) RNA, small subunit (SSU) and the presence of 5.8S rRNA or 5S rRNA depending on whether it is a eukaryotic or prokaryotic genome, respectively. Medium Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Low Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Assembly statistics include, but are not limited to total assembly size, number of contigs, contig N50/L50, and maximum contig length. For MIUVIG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities, with extensive manual review and editing to annotate putative gene functions and transcriptional units. High-quality draft genome: One or multiple fragments, totaling   90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence or predicted complete. Genome fragment(s): One or multiple fragments, totalling < 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence, or for which no genome size could be estimated

assembly_software.description: assembly software. Tool(s) used for assembly, including version number and parameters. Syntax: ^{software};{version};{parameters}$

associated_resource.description: relevant electronic resources. A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise associated to the sequence. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

association_duration.description: duration of association with the host. Time spent in host of the symbiotic organism at the time of sampling; relevant scale depends on symbiotic organism and study. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

atmospheric_data.description: atmospheric data. Measurement of atmospheric data; can include multiple data

avg_dew_point.description: average dew point. The average of dew point measures taken at the beginning of every hour over a 24 hour period on the sampling day. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

avg_occup.description: average daily occupancy. Daily average occupancy of room. Indicate the number of person(s) daily occupying the sampling room

avg_temp.description: average temperature. The average of temperatures taken at the beginning of every hour over a 24 hour period on the sampling day. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

bac_prod.value: 5 milligram per cubic meter per day
bac_prod.description: bacterial production. Bacterial production in the water column measured by isotope uptake. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

bac_resp.value: 300 micromole oxygen per liter per hour
bac_resp.description: bacterial respiration. Measurement of bacterial respiration in the water column. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

bacteria_carb_prod.description: bacterial carbon production. Measurement of bacterial carbon production. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

bacterial_density.value: 10 colony forming units per gram dry weight
bacterial_density.description: bacteria density. Number of bacteria in sample, as defined by bacteria density (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GENEPIO_0000043). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

barometric_press.description: barometric pressure. Force per unit area exerted against a surface by the weight of air above that surface. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

basin.description: basin name. Name of the basin (e.g. Campos)

bathroom_count.description: bathroom count. The number of bathrooms in the building

bedroom_count.description: bedroom count. The number of bedrooms in the building

benzene.description: benzene. Concentration of benzene in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

bin_param.description: binning parameters. The parameters that have been applied during the extraction of genomes from metagenomic datasets

bin_software.description: binning software. Tool(s) used for the extraction of genomes from metagenomic datasets, where possible include a product ID (PID) of the tool(s) used

biochem_oxygen_dem.description: biochemical oxygen demand. Amount of dissolved oxygen needed by aerobic biological organisms in a body of water to break down organic material present in a given water sample at certain temperature over a specific time period. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

biocide.description: biocide administration. List of biocides (commercial name of product and supplier) and date of administration

biocide_admin_method.description: biocide administration method. Method of biocide administration (dose, frequency, duration, time elapsed between last biociding and sampling) (e.g. 150 mg/l; weekly; 4 hr; 3 days)

biocide_used.description: biocide. Substance intended for preventing, neutralizing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating the effects of any pest or microorganism; that inhibits the growth, reproduction, and activity of organisms, including fungal cells; decreases the number of fungi or pests present; deters microbial growth and degradation of other ingredients in the formulation. Indicate the biocide used on the location where the sample was taken. Multiple terms can be separated by pipes

biol_stat.description: biological status. The level of genome modification

biomass.description: biomass. Amount of biomass; should include the name for the part of biomass measured, e.g. Microbial, total. Can include multiple measurements

biotic_regm.value: sample inoculated with Rhizobium spp. Culture
biotic_regm.description: biotic regimen. Information about treatment(s) involving use of biotic factors, such as bacteria, viruses or fungi

biotic_relationship.description: observed biotic relationship. Description of relationship(s) between the subject organism and other organism(s) it is associated with. E.g., parasite on species X; mutualist with species Y. The target organism is the subject of the relationship, and the other organism(s) is the object

birth_control.description: birth control. Specification of birth control medication used

blood_blood_disord.description: blood/blood disorder. History of blood disorders; can include multiple disorders.  The terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at http://www.disease-ontology.org, hematopoietic system disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:74)

blood_press_diast.description: host blood pressure diastolic. Resting diastolic blood pressure, measured as mm mercury. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

blood_press_syst.description: host blood pressure systolic. Resting systolic blood pressure, measured as mm mercury. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

build_docs.description: design, construction, and operation documents. The building design, construction and operation documents

build_occup_type.description: building occupancy type. The primary function for which a building or discrete part of a building is intended to be used

building_setting.description: building setting. A location (geography) where a building is set

built_struc_age.description: built structure age. The age of the built structure since construction. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

built_struc_set.description: built structure setting. The characterization of the location of the built structure as high or low human density

built_struc_type.description: built structure type. A physical structure that is a body or assemblage of bodies in space to form a system capable of supporting loads

calcium.description: calcium. Concentration of calcium in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

carb_dioxide.description: carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide (gas) amount or concentration at the time of sampling. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

carb_monoxide.description: carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide (gas) amount or concentration at the time of sampling. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

carb_nitro_ratio.description: carbon/nitrogen ratio. Ratio of amount or concentrations of carbon to nitrogen

ceil_area.description: ceiling area. The area of the ceiling space within the room. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ceil_cond.description: ceiling condition. The physical condition of the ceiling at the time of sampling; photos or video preferred; use drawings to indicate location of damaged areas

ceil_finish_mat.description: ceiling finish material. The type of material used to finish a ceiling

ceil_struc.description: ceiling structure. The construction format of the ceiling

ceil_texture.description: ceiling texture. The feel, appearance, or consistency of a ceiling surface

ceil_thermal_mass.description: ceiling thermal mass. The ability of the ceiling to provide inertia against temperature fluctuations. Generally this means concrete that is exposed. A metal deck that supports a concrete slab will act thermally as long as it is exposed to room air flow. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ceil_type.description: ceiling type. The type of ceiling according to the ceiling's appearance or construction

ceil_water_mold.description: ceiling signs of water/mold. Signs of the presence of mold or mildew on the ceiling

chem_administration.description: chemical administration. List of chemical compounds administered to the host or site where sampling occurred, and when (e.g. Antibiotics, n fertilizer, air filter); can include multiple compounds. For chemical entities of biological interest ontology (chebi) (v 163), http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/chebi

chem_mutagen.description: chemical mutagen. Treatment involving use of mutagens; should include the name of mutagen, amount administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple mutagen regimens

chem_oxygen_dem.description: chemical oxygen demand. A measure of the capacity of water to consume oxygen during the decomposition of organic matter and the oxidation of inorganic chemicals such as ammonia and nitrite. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

chem_treat_method.description: chemical treatment method. Method of chemical administration(dose, frequency, duration, time elapsed between administration and sampling) (e.g. 50 mg/l; twice a week; 1 hr; 0 days)

chem_treatment.description: chemical treatment. List of chemical compounds administered upstream the sampling location where sampling occurred (e.g. Glycols, H2S scavenger, corrosion and scale inhibitors, demulsifiers, and other production chemicals etc.). The commercial name of the product and name of the supplier should be provided. The date of administration should also be included

chimera_check.description: chimera check software. Tool(s) used for chimera checking, including version number and parameters, to discover and remove chimeric sequences. A chimeric sequence is comprised of two or more phylogenetically distinct parent sequences. Syntax: ^{software};{version};{parameters}$

chloride.description: chloride. Concentration of chloride in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

climate_environment.description: climate environment. Treatment involving an exposure to a particular climate; treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple climates

coll_site_geo_feat.description: collection site geographic feature. Text or terms that describe the geographic feature where the food sample was obtained by the researcher. This field accepts selected terms listed under the following ontologies: anthropogenic geographic feature (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000002), for example agricultural fairground [ENVO:01000986]; garden [ENVO:00000011} or any of its subclasses; market [ENVO:01000987]; water well [ENVO:01000002]; or human construction (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000070)

collection_date.description: collection date. The time of sampling, either as an instance (single point in time) or interval. In case no exact time is available, the date/time can be right truncated i.e. all of these are valid times: 2008-01-23T19:23:10+00:00; 2008-01-23T19:23:10; 2008-01-23; 2008-01; 2008; Except: 2008-01; 2008 all are ISO8601 compliant

compl_appr.description: completeness approach. The approach used to determine the completeness of a given genomic assembly, which would typically make use of a set of conserved marker genes or a closely related reference genome. For UViG completeness, include reference genome or group used, and contig feature suggesting a complete genome

compl_score.description: completeness score. Completeness score is typically based on either the fraction of markers found as compared to a database or the percent of a genome found as compared to a closely related reference genome. High Quality Draft: >90%, Medium Quality Draft: >50%, and Low Quality Draft: < 50% should have the indicated completeness scores

compl_software.description: completeness software. Tools used for completion estimate, i.e. checkm, anvi'o, busco

conduc.description: conductivity. Electrical conductivity of water. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

cons_food_stor_dur.description: food stored by consumer (storage duration). The storage duration of the food commodity by the consumer, prior to onset of illness or sample collection.  Indicate the timepoint written in ISO 8601 format. Syntax: ^{duration}$

cons_food_stor_temp.description: food stored by consumer (storage temperature). Temperature at which food commodity was stored by the consumer, prior to onset of illness or sample collection

cons_purch_date.description: purchase date. The date a food product was purchased by consumer

cons_qty_purchased.description: quantity purchased. The quantity of food purchased by consumer. Syntax: ^{integer} {text}$

contam_score.description: contamination score. The contamination score is based on the fraction of single-copy genes that are observed more than once in a query genome. The following scores are acceptable for; High Quality Draft: < 5%, Medium Quality Draft: < 10%, Low Quality Draft: < 10%. Contamination must be below 5% for a SAG or MAG to be deposited into any of the public databases

contam_screen_input.description: contamination screening input. The type of sequence data used as input

contam_screen_param.description: contamination screening parameters. Specific parameters used in the decontamination sofware, such as reference database, coverage, and kmers. Combinations of these parameters may also be used, i.e. kmer and coverage, or reference database and kmer

cool_syst_id.description: cooling system identifier. The cooling system identifier

crop_rotation.description: history/crop rotation. Whether or not crop is rotated, and if yes, rotation schedule

crop_yield.description: crop yield. Amount of crop produced per unit or area of land. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

cult_isol_date.description: culture isolation date. The datetime marking the end of a process in which a sample yields a positive result for the target microbial analyte(s) in the form of an isolated colony or colonies

cult_result.description: culture result. Any result of a bacterial culture experiment reported as a binary assessment such as positive/negative, active/inactive

cult_result_org.description: culture result organism. Taxonomic information about the cultured organism(s). Syntax: ^(({termLabel} \[{termID}\])|{integer})$

cult_root_med.description: culture rooting medium. Name or reference for the hydroponic or in vitro culture rooting medium; can be the name of a commonly used medium or reference to a specific medium, e.g. Murashige and Skoog medium. If the medium has not been formally published, use the rooting medium descriptors. Syntax: ^({text}|{PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

cult_target.description: culture target microbial analyte. The target microbial analyte in terms of investigation scope. This field accepts terms under organism (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCIT_C14250). This field also accepts identification numbers from NCBI under https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy

cur_land_use.description: current land use. Present state of sample site

cur_vegetation.description: current vegetation. Vegetation classification from one or more standard classification systems, or agricultural crop

cur_vegetation_meth.description: current vegetation method. Reference or method used in vegetation classification. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

date_extr_weath.description: extreme weather date. Date of unusual weather events that may have affected microbial populations. Multiple terms can be separated by pipes, listed in reverse chronological order

date_last_rain.description: date last rain. The date of the last time it rained

decontam_software.description: decontamination software. Tool(s) used in contamination screening

density.description: density. Density of the sample, which is its mass per unit volume (aka volumetric mass density). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

depos_env.description: depositional environment. Main depositional environment (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depositional_environment). If "other" is specified, please propose entry in "additional info" field

depth.description: depth. The vertical distance below local surface. For sediment or soil samples depth is measured from sediment or soil surface, respectively. Depth can be reported as an interval for subsurface samples. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

dermatology_disord.description: dermatology disorder. History of dermatology disorders; can include multiple disorders. The terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at http://www.disease-ontology.org, skin disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:37)

detec_type.description: detection type. Type of UViG detection

dew_point.description: dew point. The temperature to which a given parcel of humid air must be cooled, at constant barometric pressure, for water vapor to condense into water. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diet_last_six_month.description: major diet change in last six months. Specification of major diet changes in the last six months, if yes the change should be specified

dietary_claim_use.description: dietary claim or use. These descriptors are used either for foods intended for special dietary use as defined in 21 CFR 105 or for foods that have special characteristics indicated in the name or labeling. This field accepts terms listed under dietary claim or use (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03510023). Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes, but please consider limiting this list to the most prominent dietary claim or use

diether_lipids.description: diether lipids. Concentration of diether lipids; can include multiple types of diether lipids

diss_carb_dioxide.description: dissolved carbon dioxide. Concentration of dissolved carbon dioxide in the sample or liquid portion of the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_hydrogen.description: dissolved hydrogen. Concentration of dissolved hydrogen. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_inorg_carb.description: dissolved inorganic carbon. Dissolved inorganic carbon concentration in the sample, typically measured after filtering the sample using a 0.45 micrometer filter. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_inorg_nitro.description: dissolved inorganic nitrogen. Concentration of dissolved inorganic nitrogen. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_inorg_phosp.description: dissolved inorganic phosphorus. Concentration of dissolved inorganic phosphorus in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_iron.description: dissolved iron. Concentration of dissolved iron in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_org_carb.description: dissolved organic carbon. Concentration of dissolved organic carbon in the sample, liquid portion of the sample, or aqueous phase of the fluid. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_org_nitro.description: dissolved organic nitrogen. Dissolved organic nitrogen concentration measured as; total dissolved nitrogen - NH4 - NO3 - NO2. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_oxygen.description: dissolved oxygen. Concentration of dissolved oxygen. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

diss_oxygen_fluid.description: dissolved oxygen in fluids. Concentration of dissolved oxygen in the oil field produced fluids as it contributes to oxygen-corrosion and microbial activity (e.g. Mic). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

dominant_hand.description: dominant hand. Dominant hand of the subject

door_comp_type.description: door type, composite. The composite type of the door

door_cond.description: door condition. The physical condition of the door

door_direct.description: door direction of opening. The direction the door opens

door_loc.description: door location. The relative location of the door in the room

door_mat.description: door material. The material the door is composed of

door_move.description: door movement. The type of movement of the door

door_size.description: door area or size. The size of the door. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

door_type.description: door type. The type of door material

door_type_metal.description: door type, metal. The type of metal door

door_type_wood.description: door type, wood. The type of wood door

door_water_mold.description: door signs of water/mold. Signs of the presence of mold or mildew on a door

douche.description: douche. Date of most recent douche

down_par.value: 28.71 microEinstein per square meter per second
down_par.description: downward PAR. Visible waveband radiance and irradiance measurements in the water column. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

drainage_class.description: drainage classification. Drainage classification from a standard system such as the USDA system

drawings.description: drawings. The buildings architectural drawings; if design is chosen, indicate phase-conceptual, schematic, design development, and construction documents

drug_usage.description: drug usage. Any drug used by subject and the frequency of usage; can include multiple drugs used

efficiency_percent.description: efficiency percent. Percentage of volatile solids removed from the anaerobic digestor. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

elev.description: elevation. Elevation of the sampling site is its height above a fixed reference point, most commonly the mean sea level. Elevation is mainly used when referring to points on the earth's surface, while altitude is used for points above the surface, such as an aircraft in flight or a spacecraft in orbit. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

elevator.description: elevator count. The number of elevators within the built structure

emulsions.description: emulsions. Amount or concentration of substances such as paints, adhesives, mayonnaise, hair colorants, emulsified oils, etc.; can include multiple emulsion types

encoded_traits.description: encoded traits. Should include key traits like antibiotic resistance or xenobiotic degradation phenotypes for plasmids, converting genes for phage

enrichment_protocol.value: BAM Chapter 4: Enumeration of Escherichia coli and the Coliform Bacteria
enrichment_protocol.description: enrichment protocol. The microbiological workflow or protocol followed to test for the presence or enumeration of the target microbial analyte(s). Please provide a PubMed or DOI reference for published protocols. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL}|{text})$

env_broad_scale.description: broad-scale environmental context. Report the major environmental system the sample or specimen came from. The system(s) identified should have a coarse spatial grain, to provide the general environmental context of where the sampling was done (e.g. in the desert or a rainforest). We recommend using subclasses of EnvO s biome class:  http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428. EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

env_local_scale.description: local environmental context. Report the entity or entities which are in the sample or specimen s local vicinity and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample or specimen. We recommend using EnvO terms which are of smaller spatial grain than your entry for env_broad_scale. Terms, such as anatomical sites, from other OBO Library ontologies which interoperate with EnvO (e.g. UBERON) are accepted in this field. EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

env_medium.description: environmental medium. Report the environmental material(s) immediately surrounding the sample or specimen at the time of sampling. We recommend using subclasses of 'environmental material' (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00010483). EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS . Terms from other OBO ontologies are permissible as long as they reference mass/volume nouns (e.g. air, water, blood) and not discrete, countable entities (e.g. a tree, a leaf, a table top). Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

env_monitoring_zone.description: food production environmental monitoring zone. An environmental monitoring zone is a formal designation as part of an environmental monitoring program, in which areas of a food production facility are categorized, commonly as zones 1-4, based on likelihood or risk of foodborne pathogen contamination. This field accepts terms listed under food production environmental monitoring zone (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO). Please add a term to indicate the environmental monitoring zone the sample was taken from

escalator.description: escalator count. The number of escalators within the built structure

estimated_genome_size.description: estimated genome size. The estimated size of the genome prior to sequencing. Of particular importance in the sequencing of (eukaryotic) genome which could remain in draft form for a long or unspecified period

ethnicity.description: ethnicity. A category of people who identify with each other, usually on the basis of presumed similarities such as a common language, ancestry, history, society, culture, nation or social treatment within their residing area. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_contemporary_ethnic_groups

ethylbenzene.description: ethylbenzene. Concentration of ethylbenzene in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

exp_duct.description: exposed ductwork. The amount of exposed ductwork in the room. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

exp_pipe.description: exposed pipes. The number of exposed pipes in the room. Syntax: ^{integer} {text}$

experimental_factor.description: experimental factor. Variable aspects of an experiment design that can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI)

ext_door.description: exterior door count. The number of exterior doors in the built structure

ext_wall_orient.description: orientations of exterior wall. The orientation of the exterior wall

ext_window_orient.description: orientations of exterior window. The compass direction the exterior window of the room is facing

extr_weather_event.description: extreme weather event. Unusual weather events that may have affected microbial populations. Multiple terms can be separated by pipes, listed in reverse chronological order

extrachrom_elements.description: extrachromosomal elements. Do plasmids exist of significant phenotypic consequence (e.g. ones that determine virulence or antibiotic resistance). Megaplasmids? Other plasmids (borrelia has 15+ plasmids)

extreme_event.description: history/extreme events. Unusual physical events that may have affected microbial populations

facility_type.description: facility type. Establishment details about the type of facility where the sample was taken. This is independent of the specific product(s) within the facility

fao_class.description: soil_taxonomic/FAO classification. Soil classification from the FAO World soil distribution from International Soil Reference and Information Centre (ISRIC). The list of available soil classifications can be found at https://www.isric.org/explore/world-soil-distribution

farm_equip.description: farm equipment used. List of equipment used for planting, fertilization, harvesting, irrigation, land levelling, residue management, weeding or transplanting during the growing season.  This field accepts terms listed under agricultural implement (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/AGRO_00000416). Multiple terms can be separated by pipes. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

farm_equip_san.value: hot water pressure wash, hypochlorite solution, 50 parts per million
farm_equip_san.description: farm equipment sanitization. Method used to sanitize growing and harvesting equipment. This can including type and concentration of sanitizing solution.  Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes

farm_equip_san_freq.description: farm equipment sanitization frequency. The number of times farm equipment is cleaned. Frequency of cleaning might be on a Daily basis, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly or Annually

farm_equip_shared.description: equipment shared with other farms. List of planting, growing or harvesting equipment shared with other farms. This field accepts terms listed under agricultural implement (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/AGRO_00000416). Multiple terms can be separated by pipes. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

farm_water_source.description: farm watering water source. Source of water used on the farm for irrigation of crops or watering of livestock

feat_pred.description: feature prediction. Method used to predict UViGs features such as ORFs, integration site, etc. Syntax: ^{software};{version};{parameters}$

ferm_chem_add.description: fermentation chemical additives. Any chemicals that are added to the fermentation process to achieve the desired final product

ferm_chem_add_perc.description: fermentation chemical additives percentage. The amount of chemical added to the fermentation process

ferm_headspace_oxy.description: fermentation headspace oxygen. The amount of headspace oxygen in a fermentation vessel

ferm_medium.description: fermentation medium. The growth medium used for the fermented food fermentation process, which supplies the required nutrients.  Usually this includes a carbon and nitrogen source, water, micronutrients and chemical additives

ferm_pH.description: fermentation pH. The pH of the fermented food fermentation process

ferm_rel_humidity.description: fermentation relative humidity. The relative humidity of the fermented food fermentation process. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ferm_temp.description: fermentation temperature. The temperature of the fermented food fermentation process. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ferm_time.description: fermentation time. The time duration of the fermented food fermentation process. Syntax: ^{duration}$

ferm_vessel.description: fermentation vessel. The type of vessel used for containment of the fermentation

fertilizer_admin.description: fertilizer administration. Type of fertilizer or amendment added to the soil or water for the purpose of improving substrate health and quality for plant growth. This field accepts terms listed under agronomic fertilizer (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/AGRO_00002062). Multiple terms may apply and can be separated by pipes, listing in reverse chronological order. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

fertilizer_date.description: fertilizer administration date. Date of administration of soil amendment or fertilizer. Multiple terms may apply and can be separated by pipes, listing in reverse chronological order

fertilizer_regm.description: fertilizer regimen. Information about treatment involving the use of fertilizers; should include the name of fertilizer, amount administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple fertilizer regimens

field.description: field name. Name of the hydrocarbon field (e.g. Albacora)

filter_type.description: filter type. A device which removes solid particulates or airborne molecular contaminants

fire.description: history/fire. Historical and/or physical evidence of fire

fireplace_type.description: fireplace type. A firebox with chimney

flooding.description: history/flooding. Historical and/or physical evidence of flooding

floor_age.description: floor age. The time period since installment of the carpet or flooring. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

floor_area.description: floor area. The area of the floor space within the room. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

floor_cond.description: floor condition. The physical condition of the floor at the time of sampling; photos or video preferred; use drawings to indicate location of damaged areas

floor_count.description: floor count. The number of floors in the building, including basements and mechanical penthouse

floor_finish_mat.description: floor finish material. The floor covering type; the finished surface that is walked on

floor_struc.description: floor structure. Refers to the structural elements and subfloor upon which the finish flooring is installed

floor_thermal_mass.description: floor thermal mass. The ability of the floor to provide inertia against temperature fluctuations. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

floor_water_mold.description: floor signs of water/mold. Signs of the presence of mold or mildew in a room

fluor.description: fluorescence. Raw or converted fluorescence of water. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

foetal_health_stat.description: amniotic fluid/foetal health status. Specification of foetal health status, should also include abortion

food_additive.description: food additive. A substance or substances added to food to maintain or improve safety and freshness, to improve or maintain nutritional value, or improve taste, texture and appearance.  This field accepts terms listed under food additive (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03412972). Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes, but please consider limiting this list to the top 5 ingredients listed in order as on the food label.  See also, https://www.fda.gov/food/food-ingredients-packaging/overview-food-ingredients-additives-colors

food_allergen_label.value: food allergen labelling about crustaceans and products thereof [FOODON:03510215]
food_allergen_label.description: food allergen labeling. A label indication that the product contains a recognized allergen. This field accepts terms listed under dietary claim or use (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03510213)

food_clean_proc.description: food cleaning process. The process of cleaning food to separate other environmental materials from the food source. Multiple terms can be separated by pipes

food_contact_surf.description: food contact surface. The specific container or coating materials in direct contact with the food. Multiple values can be assigned.  This field accepts terms listed under food contact surface (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03500010)

food_contain_wrap.description: food container or wrapping. Type of container or wrapping defined by the main container material, the container form, and the material of the liner lids or ends. Also type of container or wrapping by form; prefer description by material first, then by form. This field accepts terms listed under food container or wrapping (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03490100)

food_cooking_proc.description: food cooking process. The transformation of raw food by the application of heat. This field accepts terms listed under food cooking (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03450002)

food_dis_point.description: food distribution point geographic location. A reference to a place on the Earth, by its name or by its geographical location that refers to a distribution point along the food chain. This field accepts terms listed under geographic location (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GAZ_00000448). Reference: Adam Diamond, James Barham. Moving Food Along the Value Chain: Innovations in Regional Food Distribution. U.S. Dept. of Agriculture, Agricultural Marketing Service. Washington, DC. March 2012. http://dx.doi.org/10.9752/MS045.03-2012. Syntax: ^{text}: {text}, {text}$

food_dis_point_city.description: food distribution point geographic location (city). A reference to a place on the Earth, by its name or by its geographical location that refers to a distribution point along the food chain. This field accepts terms listed under geographic location (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GAZ_00000448). Reference: Adam Diamond, James Barham. Moving Food Along the Value Chain: Innovations in Regional Food Distribution. U.S. Dept. of Agriculture, Agricultural Marketing Service. Washington, DC. March 2012. http://dx.doi.org/10.9752/MS045.03-2012

food_harvest_proc.description: Food harvesting process. A harvesting process is a process which takes in some food material from an individual or community of plant or animal organisms in a given context and time, and outputs a precursor or consumable food product. This may include a part of an organism or the whole, and may involve killing the organism

food_ingredient.description: food ingredient. In this field, please list individual ingredients for multi-component food [FOODON:00002501] and simple foods that is not captured in food_type.  Please use terms that are present in FoodOn.  Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes |, but please consider limiting this list to the top 5 ingredients listed in order as on the food label.  See also, https://www.fda.gov/food/food-ingredients-packaging/overview-food-ingredients-additives-colors

food_name_status.description: food product name legal status. A datum indicating that use of a food product name is regulated in some legal jurisdiction. This field accepts terms listed under food product name legal status (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03530087). Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

food_origin.description: food product origin geographic location. A reference to a place on the Earth, by its name or by its geographical location that describes the origin of the food commodity, either in terms of its cultivation or production. This field accepts terms listed under geographic location (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GAZ_00000448). Syntax: ^{text}: {text}, {text}$

food_pack_capacity.description: food package capacity. The maximum number of product units within a package. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

food_pack_integrity.description: food packing medium integrity. A term label and term id to describe the state of the packing material and text to explain the exact condition.  This field accepts terms listed under food packing medium integrity (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03530218)

food_pack_medium.description: food packing medium. The medium in which the food is packed for preservation and handling or the medium surrounding homemade foods, e.g., peaches cooked in sugar syrup. The packing medium may provide a controlled environment for the food. It may also serve to improve palatability and consumer appeal.  This includes edible packing media (e.g. fruit juice), gas other than air (e.g. carbon dioxide), vacuum packed, or packed with aerosol propellant. This field accepts terms under food packing medium (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03480020). Multiple terms may apply and can be separated by pipes

food_preserv_proc.description: food preservation process. The methods contributing to the prevention or retardation of microbial, enzymatic or oxidative spoilage and thus to the extension of shelf life. This field accepts terms listed under food preservation process (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03470107)

food_prior_contact.description: material of contact prior to food packaging. The material the food contacted (e.g., was processed in) prior to packaging. This field accepts terms listed under material of contact prior to food packaging (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03530077). If the proper descriptor is not listed please use text to describe the material of contact prior to food packaging

food_prod.description: food production system characteristics. Descriptors of the food production system or of the agricultural environment and growing conditions related to the farm production system, such as wild caught, organic, free-range, industrial, dairy, beef,  domestic or cultivated food production. This field accepts terms listed under food production (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03530206). Multiple terms may apply and can be separated by pipes. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

food_prod_char.description: food production characteristics. Descriptors of the food production system such as wild caught, free-range, organic, free-range, industrial, dairy, beef

food_prod_synonym.description: food product synonym. Other names by which the food product is known by (e.g., regional or non-English names)

food_product_qual.description: food product by quality. Descriptors for describing food visually or via other senses, which is useful for tasks like food inspection where little prior knowledge of how the food came to be is available. Some terms like "food (frozen)" are both a quality descriptor and the output of a process. This field accepts terms listed under food product by quality (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_00002454). Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

food_product_type.description: food product type. A food product type is a class of food products that is differentiated by its food composition (e.g., single- or multi-ingredient), processing and/or consumption characteristics. This does not include brand name products but it may include generic food dish categories. This field accepts terms under food product type (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON:03400361). For terms related to food product for an animal, consult food product for animal (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03309997). If the proper descriptor is not listed please use text to describe the food type. Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes

food_quality_date.description: food quality date. The date recommended for the use of the product while at peak quality, this date is not a reflection of safety unless used on infant formula this date is not a reflection of safety and is typically labeled on a food product as "best if used by," best by," "use by," or "freeze by."

food_source.description: food source. Type of plant or animal from which the food product or its major ingredient is derived or a chemical food source [FDA CFSAN 1995]

food_source_age.description: food source age. The age of the food source host organism. Depending on the type of host organism, age may be more appropriate to report in days, weeks, or years. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

food_trace_list.description: food traceability list category. The FDA is proposing to establish additional traceability recordkeeping requirements (beyond what is already required in existing regulations) for persons who manufacture, process, pack, or hold foods the Agency has designated for inclusion on the Food Traceability List. The Food Traceability List (FTL) identifies the foods for which the additional traceability records described in the proposed rule would be required. The term  Food Traceability List  (FTL) refers not only to the foods specifically listed (https://www.fda.gov/media/142303/download), but also to any foods that contain listed foods as ingredients

food_trav_mode.description: food shipping transportation method. A descriptor for the method of movement of food commodity along the food distribution system.  This field accepts terms listed under travel mode (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GENEPIO_0001064). If the proper descrptor is not listed please use text to describe the mode of travel. Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

food_trav_vehic.description: food shipping transportation vehicle. A descriptor for the mobile machine which is used to transport food commodities along the food distribution system.  This field accepts terms listed under vehicle (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_01000604). If the proper descrptor is not listed please use text to describe the mode of travel. Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes

food_treat_proc.description: food treatment process. Used to specifically characterize a food product based on the treatment or processes applied to the product or any indexed ingredient. The processes include adding, substituting or removing components or modifying the food or component, e.g., through fermentation. Multiple values can be assigned. This fields accepts terms listed under food treatment process (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/FOODON_03460111)

freq_clean.description: frequency of cleaning. The number of times the sample location is cleaned. Frequency of cleaning might be on a Daily basis, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly or Annually

freq_cook.description: frequency of cooking. The number of times a meal is cooked per week. Syntax: ^{integer} {text}$

fungicide_regm.description: fungicide regimen. Information about treatment involving use of fungicides; should include the name of fungicide, amount administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple fungicide regimens

furniture.description: furniture. The types of furniture present in the sampled room

gaseous_environment.description: gaseous environment. Use of conditions with differing gaseous environments; should include the name of gaseous compound, amount administered, treatment duration, interval and total experimental duration; can include multiple gaseous environment regimens

gaseous_substances.description: gaseous substances. Amount or concentration of substances such as hydrogen sulfide, carbon dioxide, methane, etc.; can include multiple substances

gastrointest_disord.description: gastrointestinal tract disorder. History of gastrointestinal tract disorders; can include multiple disorders. History of blood disorders; can include multiple disorders.  The terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at http://www.disease-ontology.org, gastrointestinal system disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:77)

gender_restroom.description: gender of restroom. The gender type of the restroom

genetic_mod.description: genetic modification. Genetic modifications of the genome of an organism, which may occur naturally by spontaneous mutation, or be introduced by some experimental means, e.g. specification of a transgene or the gene knocked-out or details of transient transfection. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

geo_loc_name.description: geographic location (country and/or sea,region). The geographical origin of the sample as defined by the country or sea name followed by specific region name. Country or sea names should be chosen from the INSDC country list (http://insdc.org/country.html), or the GAZ ontology (http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/GAZ). Syntax: ^{country}: {region}, {specific_location}$

gestation_state.description: amniotic fluid/gestation state. Specification of the gestation state

glucosidase_act.description: glucosidase activity. Measurement of glucosidase activity. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

gravidity.description: gravidity. Whether or not subject is gravid, and if yes date due or date post-conception, specifying which is used

gravity.description: gravity. Information about treatment involving use of gravity factor to study various types of responses in presence, absence or modified levels of gravity; treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple treatments

growth_facil.description: growth facility. Type of facility where the sampled plant was grown; controlled vocabulary: growth chamber, open top chamber, glasshouse, experimental garden, field. Alternatively use Crop Ontology (CO) terms, see http://www.cropontology.org/ontology/CO_715/Crop%20Research

growth_habit.description: growth habit. Characteristic shape, appearance or growth form of a plant species

growth_hormone_regm.description: growth hormone regimen. Information about treatment involving use of growth hormones; should include the name of growth hormone, amount administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple growth hormone regimens

growth_medium.description: growth medium. A liquid or gel containing nutrients, salts, and other factors formulated to support the growth of microorganisms, cells, or plants (National Cancer Institute Thesaurus).  The name of the medium used to grow the microorganism

gynecologic_disord.description: gynecological disorder. History of gynecological disorders; can include multiple disorders. The terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at http://www.disease-ontology.org, female reproductive system disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:229)

hall_count.description: hallway/corridor count. The total count of hallways and corridors in the built structure

handidness.description: handidness. The handidness of the individual sampled

hc_produced.description: hydrocarbon type produced. Main hydrocarbon type produced from resource (i.e. Oil, gas, condensate, etc). If "other" is specified, please propose entry in "additional info" field

hcr.description: hydrocarbon resource type. Main Hydrocarbon Resource type. The term "Hydrocarbon Resource" HCR defined as a natural environmental feature containing large amounts of hydrocarbons at high concentrations potentially suitable for commercial exploitation. This term should not be confused with the Hydrocarbon Occurrence term which also includes hydrocarbon-rich environments with currently limited commercial interest such as seeps, outcrops, gas hydrates etc. If "other" is specified, please propose entry in "additional info" field

hcr_fw_salinity.description: formation water salinity. Original formation water salinity (prior to secondary recovery e.g. Waterflooding) expressed as TDS. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

hcr_geol_age.description: hydrocarbon resource geological age. Geological age of hydrocarbon resource (Additional info: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_(geology)). If "other" is specified, please propose entry in "additional info" field

hcr_pressure.description: hydrocarbon resource original pressure. Original pressure of the hydrocarbon resource. Syntax: ^{float} *- *{float} {unit}$

hcr_temp.description: hydrocarbon resource original temperature. Original temperature of the hydrocarbon resource. Syntax: ^{float} *- *{float} {unit}$

heat_cool_type.description: heating and cooling system type. Methods of conditioning or heating a room or building

heat_deliv_loc.description: heating delivery locations. The location of heat delivery within the room

heat_sys_deliv_meth.description: heating system delivery method. The method by which the heat is delivered through the system

heat_system_id.description: heating system identifier. The heating system identifier

heavy_metals.description: extreme_unusual_properties/heavy metals. Heavy metals present in the sequenced sample and their concentrations. For multiple heavy metals and concentrations, add multiple copies of this field

heavy_metals_meth.description: extreme_unusual_properties/heavy metals method. Reference or method used in determining heavy metals. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

height_carper_fiber.description: height carpet fiber mat. The average carpet fiber height in the indoor environment. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

herbicide_regm.description: herbicide regimen. Information about treatment involving use of herbicides; information about treatment involving use of growth hormones; should include the name of herbicide, amount administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple regimens

horizon_meth.description: horizon method. Reference or method used in determining the horizon. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

host_age.description: host age. Age of host at the time of sampling; relevant scale depends on species and study, e.g. Could be seconds for amoebae or centuries for trees. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_body_habitat.description: host body habitat. Original body habitat where the sample was obtained from

host_body_mass_index.description: host body-mass index. Body mass index, calculated as weight/(height)squared. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_body_product.description: host body product. Substance produced by the body, e.g. Stool, mucus, where the sample was obtained from. Use terms from the foundational model of anatomy ontology (fma) or Uber-anatomy ontology (UBERON)

host_body_site.description: host body site. Name of body site where the sample was obtained from, such as a specific organ or tissue (tongue, lung etc...). Use terms from the foundational model of anatomy ontology (fma) or the Uber-anatomy ontology (UBERON)

host_body_temp.description: host body temperature. Core body temperature of the host when sample was collected. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_cellular_loc.description: host cellular location. The localization of the symbiotic host organism within the host from which it was sampled: e.g. intracellular if the symbiotic host organism is localized within the cells or extracellular if the symbiotic host organism is localized outside of cells

host_color.description: host color. The color of host

host_common_name.description: host common name. Common name of the host

host_dependence.description: host dependence. Type of host dependence for the symbiotic host organism to its host

host_diet.description: host diet. Type of diet depending on the host, for animals omnivore, herbivore etc., for humans high-fat, meditteranean etc.; can include multiple diet types

host_disease_stat.description: host disease status. List of diseases with which the host has been diagnosed; can include multiple diagnoses. The value of the field depends on host; for humans the terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at https://www.disease-ontology.org, non-human host diseases are free text

host_dry_mass.description: host dry mass. Measurement of dry mass. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_fam_rel.description: host family relationship. Relationships to other hosts in the same study; can include multiple relationships

host_growth_cond.description: host growth conditions. Literature reference giving growth conditions of the host. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL}|{text})$

host_height.description: host height. The height of subject. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_hiv_stat.description: host HIV status. HIV status of subject, if yes HAART initiation status should also be indicated as [YES or NO]

host_infra_spec_name.description: host infra-specific name. Taxonomic information about the host below subspecies level

host_infra_spec_rank.description: host infra-specific rank. Taxonomic rank information about the host below subspecies level, such as variety, form, rank etc

host_last_meal.description: host last meal. Content of last meal and time since feeding; can include multiple values

host_length.description: host length. The length of subject. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_life_stage.description: host life stage. Description of life stage of host

host_number.description: host number individual. Number of symbiotic host individuals pooled at the time of collection

host_occupation.description: host occupation. Most frequent job performed by subject

host_of_host_coinf.description: observed coinfecting organisms in host of host. The taxonomic name of any coinfecting organism observed in a symbiotic relationship with the host of the sampled host organism. e.g. where a sample collected from a host trematode species (A) which was collected from a host_of_host fish (B) that was also infected with a nematode (C), the value here would be (C) the nematode {species name} or {common name}. Multiple co-infecting species may be added in a comma-separated list. For listing symbiotic organisms associated with the host (A) use the term Observed host symbiont

host_of_host_disease.description: host of the symbiotic host disease status. List of diseases with which the host of the symbiotic host organism has been diagnosed; can include multiple diagnoses. The value of the field depends on host; for humans the terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at https://www.disease-ontology.org, non-human host diseases are free text

host_of_host_env_loc.description: host of the symbiotic host local environmental context. For a symbiotic host organism the local anatomical environment within its host may have causal influences. Report the anatomical entity(s) which are in the direct environment of the symbiotic host organism being sampled and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample or specimen. For example, if the symbiotic host organism being sampled is an intestinal worm, its local environmental context will be the term for intestine from UBERON (http://uberon.github.io/)

host_of_host_env_med.description: host of the symbiotic host environmental medium. Report the environmental material(s) immediately surrounding the symbiotic host organism at the time of sampling. This usually will be a tissue or substance type from the host, but may be another material if the symbiont is external to the host. We recommend using classes from the UBERON ontology, but subclasses of 'environmental material' (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00010483) may also be used. EnvO documentation about how to use the field: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS . Terms from other OBO ontologies are permissible as long as they reference mass/volume nouns (e.g. air, water, blood) and not discrete, countable entities (e.g. intestines, heart).MIxS . Terms from other OBO ontologies are permissible as long as they reference mass/volume nouns (e.g. air, water, blood) and not discrete, countable entities (e.g. intestines, heart)

host_of_host_fam_rel.description: host of the symbiotic host family relationship. Familial relationship of the host of the symbiotic host organisms to other hosts of symbiotic host organism in the same study; can include multiple relationships

host_of_host_geno.description: host of the symbiotic host genotype. Observed genotype of the host of the symbiotic host organism

host_of_host_gravid.description: host of the symbiotic host gravidity. Whether or not the host of the symbiotic host organism is gravid, and if yes date due or date post-conception, specifying which is used

host_of_host_infname.description: host of the symbiotic host infra-specific name. Taxonomic name information of the host of the symbiotic host organism below subspecies level

host_of_host_infrank.description: host of the symbiotic host infra-specific rank. Taxonomic rank information about the host of the symbiotic host organism below subspecies level, such as variety, form, rank etc

host_of_host_name.description: host of the symbiotic host common name. Common name of the host of the symbiotic host organism

host_of_host_pheno.description: host of the symbiotic host phenotype. Phenotype of the host of the symbiotic host organism. For phenotypic quality ontology (PATO) terms, see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/pato

host_of_host_sub_id.description: host of the symbiotic host subject id. A unique identifier by which each host of the symbiotic host organism subject can be referred to, de-identified, e.g. #H14

host_of_host_taxid.description: host of the symbiotic host taxon id. NCBI taxon id of the host of the symbiotic host organism

host_of_host_totmass.description: host of the symbiotic host total mass. Total mass of the host of the symbiotic host organism at collection, the unit depends on the host. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_phenotype.description: host phenotype. Phenotype of human or other host. Use terms from the phenotypic quality ontology (pato) or the Human Phenotype Ontology (HP)

host_pred_appr.description: host prediction approach. Tool or approach used for host prediction

host_pred_est_acc.value: CRISPR spacer match: 0 or 1 mismatches, estimated 8% FDR at the host genus rank (Edwards et al. 2016 doi:10.1093/femsre/fuv048)
host_pred_est_acc.description: host prediction estimated accuracy. For each tool or approach used for host prediction, estimated false discovery rates should be included, either computed de novo or from the literature

host_pulse.description: host pulse. Resting pulse, measured as beats per minute. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_sex.description: host sex. Gender or physical sex of the host

host_shape.description: host shape. Morphological shape of host

host_spec_range.description: host specificity or range. The range and diversity of host species that an organism is capable of infecting, defined by NCBI taxonomy identifier

host_specificity.description: host specificity. Level of specificity of symbiont-host interaction: e.g. generalist (symbiont able to establish associations with distantly related hosts) or species-specific

host_subject_id.description: host subject id. A unique identifier by which each subject can be referred to, de-identified

host_subspecf_genlin.description: host subspecific genetic lineage. Information about the genetic distinctness of the host organism below the subspecies level e.g., serovar, serotype, biotype, ecotype, variety, cultivar, or any relevant genetic typing schemes like Group I plasmid. Subspecies should not be recorded in this term, but in the NCBI taxonomy. Supply both the lineage name and the lineage rank separated by a colon, e.g., biovar:abc123

host_substrate.description: host substrate. The growth substrate of the host

host_symbiont.description: observed host symbionts. The taxonomic name of the organism(s) found living in mutualistic, commensalistic, or parasitic symbiosis with the specific host. The sampled symbiont can have its own symbionts. For example, parasites may have hyperparasites (=parasites of the parasite)

host_taxid.description: host taxid. NCBI taxon id of the host, e.g. 9606

host_tot_mass.description: host total mass. Total mass of the host at collection, the unit depends on host. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

host_wet_mass.description: host wet mass. Measurement of wet mass. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

hrt.description: HRT. Whether subject had hormone replacement theraphy, and if yes start date

humidity.description: humidity. Amount of water vapour in the air, at the time of sampling. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

humidity_regm.description: humidity regimen. Information about treatment involving an exposure to varying degree of humidity; information about treatment involving use of growth hormones; should include amount of humidity administered, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple regimens

hygienic_area.description: hygienic food production area. The subdivision of areas within a food production facility according to hygienic requirements. This field accepts terms listed under hygienic food production area (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO). Please add a term that most accurately indicates the hygienic area your sample was taken from according to the definitions provided

hysterectomy.description: hysterectomy. Specification of whether hysterectomy was performed

ihmc_medication_code.description: IHMC medication code. Can include multiple medication codes

indoor_space.description: indoor space. A distinguishable space within a structure, the purpose for which discrete areas of a building is used

indoor_surf.description: indoor surface. Type of indoor surface

indust_eff_percent.description: industrial effluent percent. Percentage of industrial effluents received by wastewater treatment plant. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$
