tot_nitro_cont_meth.description: total nitrogen content method. Reference or method used in determining the total nitrogen. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

tot_nitro_content.value: 35 milligrams Nitrogen per kilogram of soil
tot_nitro_content.description: total nitrogen content. Total nitrogen content of the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tot_org_c_meth.description: total organic carbon method. Reference or method used in determining total organic carbon. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

tot_org_carb.description: total organic carbon. Total organic carbon content. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tot_part_carb.description: total particulate carbon. Total particulate carbon content. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tot_phosp.description: total phosphorus. Total phosphorus concentration in the sample, calculated by: total phosphorus = total dissolved phosphorus + particulate phosphorus. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tot_phosphate.description: total phosphate. Total amount or concentration of phosphate. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tot_sulfur.description: total sulfur. Concentration of total sulfur in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

train_line.description: train line. The subway line name

train_stat_loc.description: train station collection location. The train station collection location

train_stop_loc.description: train stop collection location. The train stop collection location

travel_out_six_month.description: travel outside the country in last six months. Specification of the countries travelled in the last six months; can include multiple travels

trna_ext_software.description: tRNA extraction software. Tools used for tRNA identification. Syntax: ^{software};{version};{parameters}$

trnas.description: number of standard tRNAs extracted. The total number of tRNAs identified from the SAG or MAG

trophic_level.description: trophic level. Trophic levels are the feeding position in a food chain. Microbes can be a range of producers (e.g. chemolithotroph)

turbidity.description: turbidity. Measure of the amount of cloudiness or haziness in water caused by individual particles. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tvdss_of_hcr_press.description: depth (TVDSS) of hydrocarbon resource pressure. True vertical depth subsea (TVDSS) of the hydrocarbon resource where the original pressure was measured (e.g. 1578 m). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

tvdss_of_hcr_temp.description: depth (TVDSS) of hydrocarbon resource temperature. True vertical depth subsea (TVDSS) of the hydrocarbon resource where the original temperature was measured (e.g. 1345 m). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

twin_sibling.description: twin sibling presence. Specification of twin sibling presence

typ_occup_density.description: typical occupant density. Customary or normal density of occupants

type_of_symbiosis.description: type of symbiosis. Type of biological interaction established between the symbiotic host organism being sampled and its respective host

urine_collect_meth.description: urine/collection method. Specification of urine collection method

urobiom_sex.description: urobiome sex. Physical sex of the host

urogenit_disord.description: urogenital disorder. History of urogenital disorders, can include multiple disorders. The terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at http://www.disease-ontology.org, reproductive system disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:15) or urinary system disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:18)

urogenit_tract_disor.description: urine/urogenital tract disorder. History of urogenital tract disorders; can include multiple disorders. The terms should be chosen from the DO (Human Disease Ontology) at http://www.disease-ontology.org, urinary system disease (https://disease-ontology.org/?id=DOID:18)

ventilation_rate.description: ventilation rate. Ventilation rate of the system in the sampled premises. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

ventilation_type.description: ventilation type. Ventilation system used in the sampled premises

vfa.description: volatile fatty acids. Concentration of Volatile Fatty Acids in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

vfa_fw.description: vfa in formation water. Original volatile fatty acid concentration in the hydrocarbon resource. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

vir_ident_software.description: viral identification software. Tool(s) used for the identification of UViG as a viral genome, software or protocol name including version number, parameters, and cutoffs used

virus_enrich_appr.description: virus enrichment approach. List of approaches used to enrich the sample for viruses, if any

vis_media.description: visual media. The building visual media

viscosity.description: viscosity. A measure of oil's resistance to gradual deformation by shear stress or tensile stress (e.g. 3.5 cp; 100 °C)

volatile_org_comp.description: volatile organic compounds. Concentration of carbon-based chemicals that easily evaporate at room temperature; can report multiple volatile organic compounds by entering numeric values preceded by name of compound

wall_area.description: wall area. The total area of the sampled room's walls. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

wall_const_type.description: wall construction type. The building class of the wall defined by the composition of the building elements and fire-resistance rating

wall_finish_mat.description: wall finish material. The material utilized to finish the outer most layer of the wall

wall_height.description: wall height. The average height of the walls in the sampled room. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

wall_loc.description: wall location. The relative location of the wall within the room

wall_surf_treatment.description: wall surface treatment. The surface treatment of interior wall

wall_texture.description: wall texture. The feel, appearance, or consistency of a wall surface

wall_thermal_mass.description: wall thermal mass. The ability of the wall to provide inertia against temperature fluctuations. Generally this means concrete or concrete block that is either exposed or covered only with paint. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

wall_water_mold.description: wall signs of water/mold. Signs of the presence of mold or mildew on a wall

wastewater_type.description: wastewater type. The origin of wastewater such as human waste, rainfall, storm drains, etc

water_cont_soil_meth.description: water content method. Reference or method used in determining the water content of soil. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

water_content.description: water content. Water content measurement. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

water_current.description: water current. Measurement of magnitude and direction of flow within a fluid. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

water_cut.description: water cut. Current amount of water (%) in a produced fluid stream; or the average of the combined streams. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

water_feat_size.description: water feature size. The size of the water feature. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

water_feat_type.description: water feature type. The type of water feature present within the building being sampled

water_frequency.description: water delivery frequency. Number of water delivery events within a given period of time

water_pH.description: water pH. pH measurement of some water at the time of sampling

water_prod_rate.description: water production rate. Water production rates per well (e.g. 987 m3 / day). Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

water_source_adjac.description: environmental feature adjacent water source. Description of the environmental features that are adjacent to the farm water source. This field accepts terms under ecosystem (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_01001110) and human construction (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000070). Multiple terms can be separated by pipes

water_source_shared.description: water source shared. Other users sharing access to the same water source. Multiple terms can be separated by one or more pipes

water_temp_regm.description: water temperature regimen. Information about treatment involving an exposure to water with varying degree of temperature, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple regimens

watering_regm.description: watering regimen. Information about treatment involving an exposure to watering frequencies, treatment regimen including how many times the treatment was repeated, how long each treatment lasted, and the start and end time of the entire treatment; can include multiple regimens

weekday.description: weekday. The day of the week when sampling occurred

weight_loss_3_month.description: weight loss in last three months. Specification of weight loss in the last three months, if yes should be further specified to include amount of weight loss

wga_amp_appr.description: WGA amplification approach. Method used to amplify genomic DNA in preparation for sequencing

wga_amp_kit.description: WGA amplification kit. Kit used to amplify genomic DNA in preparation for sequencing

win.description: well identification number. A unique identifier of a well or wellbore. This is part of the Global Framework for Well Identification initiative which is compiled by the Professional Petroleum Data Management Association (PPDM) in an effort to improve well identification systems. (Supporting information: https://ppdm.org/ and http://dl.ppdm.org/dl/690)

wind_direction.description: wind direction. Wind direction is the direction from which a wind originates

wind_speed.description: wind speed. speed of wind measured at the time of sampling. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

window_cond.description: window condition. The physical condition of the window at the time of sampling

window_cover.description: window covering. The type of window covering

window_horiz_pos.description: window horizontal position. The horizontal position of the window on the wall

window_loc.description: window location. The relative location of the window within the room

window_mat.description: window material. The type of material used to finish a window

window_open_freq.description: window open frequency. The number of times windows are opened per week

window_size.description: window area/size. The window's length and width

window_status.description: window status. Defines whether the windows were open or closed during environmental testing

window_type.description: window type. The type of windows

window_vert_pos.description: window vertical position. The vertical position of the window on the wall

window_water_mold.description: window signs of water/mold. Signs of the presence of mold or mildew on the window

x16s_recover.description: 16S recovered. Can a 16S gene be recovered from the submitted SAG or MAG?

x16s_recover_software.description: 16S recovery software. Tools used for 16S rRNA gene extraction. Syntax: ^{software};{version};{parameters}$

xylene.description: xylene. Concentration of xylene in the sample. Syntax: ^{scientific_float}( *- *{scientific_float})? *{text}$

isotope.description: isotope. The element and mass number of the stable isotope used in isotopologue labeling.

isotopolog.description: isotopolog. Isotopologue (isotope source/substrate/molecule) added to the biological sample.. Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

isotopolog_label.description: isotopolog label status. List whether the isotopologue added to this biological sample was heavy-labelled or natural abundance

isotopolog_approach.description: Labeling approach (number of labeled isotopologs supplied). The labelling approach of this SIP experiment. Details if multiple isotopically labelled isotopologues were added to samples ("multiple"), or was only one isotopologue added to each sample ("single").

gradient_position.description: gradient position. A number designating the gradient position from heaviest (=1) to lightest. Unfractionated samples, from which fractionated samples were derived, should be denoted with –1.

gradient_pos_density.description: density of gradient position. Buoyant density of this fraction. Syntax: ^({float}-{float} {unit}|{float} {unit})$

gradient_pos_rel_am.description: relative amount of nucleic acids in the gradient position. The total nucleic acids loaded onto the column in this fraction as a decimal. If uploading 16S rRNA gene (or other amplicon) sequencing data, this value should be calculated from qPCR data. If uploading untargetted sequencing data, this value should be calculated from total DNA concentration.. Syntax: ^{float}$

sip_method.description: method for SIP fractionating. Method used to fractionate nucleic acids.. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

isotopolog_atom_frac.description: atom fraction of isotopolog. The fraction of heavy-labelled atoms out of all atoms of a given element in the isotopolog. Multiple values allowed, separated by a | and should be orded the same as the isotopolog.

isotopolog_atom_pos.description: set of labeled atoms in isotopologue. InChI label designating set of all isotopically enriched atoms in isotopologue. Multiple values allowed, separated by a | and should be orded the same as the isotopolog.. Syntax: ^({termLabel} \[{termID}\]|{text})$

isotopolog_dose.description: dose of isotopolog. The concentration (in ppm) of isotopolog added to environmental matrix as a total mass per volume.. Syntax: ^{float} {unit}$

nucleobase_atom_frac.description: nucleobase excess atom fraction. Excess atom fraction of the nucleobases in this fraction.

isotopolog_incu_time.description: isotopolog incubation time. Total time of incubation after isotopologue addition in hours. Syntax: ^{float} {unit}$

internal_standard.description: internal standard method. Method used for internal standard for SIP fractionation, if an internal standard was used (i.e., spiking in a heavy-labelled DNA sequence).. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

samp_dna_conc.description: sample dna concentration. DNA concentration of sample after dna extraction prior to pooling. Typically measured spectrophotometrically or with a fluorophore.. Syntax: ^{float} {unit}$

nucleic_acid_elution_vol.description: nucleic acid elution volume. Volume the nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) sample is eluted in. Syntax: ^{float} {unit}$

orig_site_name.description: name of site or location where sample originated. Designated name of the archaeological or ecological site, ancient settlement, or location etc. where the sample was originally collected. Can be a non-geographical name, such as a field-specific name or code, the official name of an excavation, or a colloquial name that is used in academic literature. Typically names that would not be found on official maps. If the site name is unclear please use the name of the closest location or region as best as possible. Can also include different transliterations or languages used in the literature.

orig_site_loc.description: original site location. The original geographical origin of the sample, when sampled outside its original natural environment (e.g. sampled in a museum collection), as defined by the country or sea name followed by specific region name.  Country or sea names should be chosen from the INSDC country list (http://insdc.org/country.html), or the GAZ ontology (http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/GAZ).. Syntax: ^{country}: {region}, {specific_location}$

orig_site_lat.description: original geographic location (latitude). The latitude coordinate of the original geographical origin of the sample, e.g. the original place the sample was buried, deposited, or formed. In cases where the sample was directly sampled in the burial environment for the purposes of scientific investigation, this will be the same as geo_loc_name, and lat_lon. For samples kept in collections, the geo_loc_name and lat_lon terms are used to refer to the collection where the sample is stored, but this term is used for the original geographic location the sample existed in prior to archiving in a collection (i.e., should correspond to  orig_site_loc, not the collection itself as recorded in site_name). The values should be reported in decimal degrees, limited to 8 decimal points, and in WGS84 system.. Syntax: ^{lat}$

orig_site_lon.description: original geographic location (longitude). The longitude coordinate of the original geographical origin of the sample, e.g. the original place the sample was buried, deposited, or formed. In cases where the sample was directly sampled in the burial environment for the purposes of scientific investigation, this will be the same as geo_loc_name, and lat_lon. For samples kept in collections, the geo_loc_name and lat_lon terms are used to refer to the collection where the sample is stored, but this term is used for the original geographic location the sample existed in prior to archiving in a collection (i.e., should correspond to orig_site_loc, not the collection itself, as recorded in site_name). The values should be reported in decimal degrees, limited to 8 decimal points, and in WGS84 system.. Syntax: ^{lon}$

past_env_broad.description: broad-scale past environmental context. Report information about the general ancient broad environmental system that the sample or specimen existed or lived within, as it was at the time of deposition or burial (e.g. in the desert or a forest). This should not describe the environment as it is today (e.g. farmland), but specifically the state as it was in the past (i.e. the palaeo- or (pre)historical ecosystem). Compared to `env_broad_scale` which is taken from direct observation, the information about the past environment will normally be derived from inference from archaeological, palaeontological, geological, or other scientific methods. We recommend using subclasses of EnvO s biome class:  http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428. EnvO documentation about how to use the field for present day equivalents: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS\"". Syntax: ^{termLabel} \[{termID}\]$

past_env_local.description: local past environmental context. Report information about the smaller-scale environmental system of the local vicinity of the sample or specimen at the time of deposition or burial (e.g. in hillside, burial mound, or midden). This should not describe the environment as it is today (e.g. carpark), but specifically the entity or entities surrounding the sample that may have significant causal influences as it was in the past. Compared to `env_local_scale` which is taken from direct observation, the information about the past environment will normally be derived from inference from archaeological, palaeontological, geological, or other scientific methods. We recommend using EnvO terms which are of smaller than your entry for past_env_broad. Terms, such as anatomical sites, from other OBO Library ontologies which interoperate with EnvO (e.g. UBERON) are accepted in this field. EnvO documentation about how to use the field for present day equivalents: https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/wiki/Using-ENVO-with-MIxS\

stratigraph_context.description: stratigraphic context. Associated stratigraphic context(s) that the sample was retrieved from, usually from an archaeological or palaeontological excavation. Description(s) or identifier(s) of stratigraphic units or layer names within and/or relative to the site (e.g., stratigraphic unit ID, archaeological feature ID, layer name or a description, grid location).

context_retrieval_date.description: date of retrieval from depositional context. Date of excavation or retrieval from burial or depositional context, if known. If excavations were done during a  longer period, report its midpoint at a month or year level. In case no exact time is available, the date can be  right truncated i.e. all of these are valid times: 2008-01-23T19:23:10+00:00; 2008-01-23T19:23:10; 2008-01-23;  2008-01; 2008; Except: 2008-01; 2008 all are ISO8601 compliant.

permit_id.description: permit or approval ID. A permit ID, code, or any form of identify provided by any authority (ethical, local, legal, academic etc.) associated with the approval of the analysis of this particular sample, if available.

permit_authority.description: permit authority. Name of the authorit(ies) or institution(s) that granted sampling and analysis (e.g. human remains) and/or export permission (e.g. animal remains), as well any form of ethical approval (whether from institutional research ethics boards such as REB or IRBs, or indigenous or native community associations), if available.

permit_date.description: date of permit approval. Date on which a permit was granted. The date can be right truncated i.e. all of these are valid times: 2008-01-23; 2008-01; 2008; Except: 2008-01; 2008 all are ISO8601 compliant.

permit_scope.value: Defined scope only includes the study of bacterial sequences and any human sequence is not covered under the agreement.
permit_scope.description: permit scope. Description of the original scope and permissions of the research on the genetic material, as was approved by a legal, ethical, or relevant authority (e.g. bacteria only, DNA only, bacteria and human, no host read analysis allowed). Note this description is only informative, and will not necessarily automatically apply restrictions to associated data to other researchers.

biocultural_label.description: biocultural label. Relevant biocultural labels defined by the local contexts project (https://localcontexts.org/label/bc-provenance/) that describe in what ways this data can be reused, as permitted by any associated native or indigenous peoples or communities.

samp_alt_lab_ids.description: alternative sample IDs. An alternative sample or material ID related to the sample not already covered by terms samp_name and source_mat_id, including from associated other non-genetic analyses of the same sample, that can be used synonymously with the main ID. For example: external database IDs, internal lab sample ID from sampling such as bone drilling, or IDs from other scientific analyses. Can be specified multiple times for different ID contexts.

prev_pubs.description: previous publications. Any previous publications that report non-nucleic acid data from the same sample or ultimate source of the sample. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

host_preserv_state.description: preservation state of sampled host at death. Description of the state of the sampled (ancient) organism/host as originally  preserved in the burial environment at the time of or immediately following death. This can be both natural or artificial, such as mummification or burning for funerary purposes.

samp_preserv_treatm.description: preservational treatment. Description of any treatment applied directly to samples for the specific purpose of  maximising longevity of sample preservation in archives and/or collections by curators  that may influence downstream nucleic acid recovery or library construction, such as storage fluid or  reconstructive glue.

cultural_era.description: cultural era or period. The cultural era approximating to the period in which the archaeological remains existed in. Where possible use terms from ontologies such as Chronontology (https://chronontology.dainst.org/) or PeriodO (https://perio.do/en/).

geological_epoch.description: geological epoch. The geological epoch approximating to the period within which the specimen or sample existed. Where possible use terms from ontologies. NOTE: This term is for geological timescales. For more precise or anthropogenic defined periods, use `Cultural Era`.

earliest_chrono_age.description: earliest chronometric age. The maximum/earliest/oldest possible age of a specimen as determined by a dating method. If multiple dating measurements available, use the most earliest/oldest date to provide widest range of age possibilities. The specific age unit should be specified by the term earliest_chrono_sys. More information on specific dates (e.g. radiocarbon lab codes) can be specified in the term chrono_age_remarks.

earliest_chrono_sys.description: earliest chronometric age reference system. The reference system associated with the earliest_chrono_age.

latest_chrono_age.description: latest chronometric age. The minimum/latest/youngest possible age of a specimen as determined by a dating method. If multiple dating measurements available, use the most latest/youngest date to provide widest range of age possibilities. The specific age unit should be specified by the term latest_chrono_sys. More information on specific dates (e.g. radiocarbon lab codes) can be specified in the term chrono_age_remarks.

latest_chrono_sys.description: latest chronometric age reference system. The reference system associated with the latest_chrono_age.

chrono_age_protocol.description: chronometric age protocol. A description of or reference to the methods used to determine the earliest_chrono_age and latest_chrono_age.

chrono_age_remarks.value: radiocarbon dating, calibrated with OxCal v4.3 with 95% confidence interval
chrono_age_remarks.description: chronometric age remarks. Notes or comments about the  earliest_chrono_age and latest_chrono_age. For more detail use Chronometric Age Protocol to point to original publication describing method. Useful to specify confidence and/or accuracy of reported date.

palaeopath_status.description: palaeopathology status. Describe briefly any relevant palaeopathological or health-related observations of the remains of the individual or subject under study.

batch_ids.description: batch identifiers. Identifiers for any form of batch or 'group' that the samples is associated with, examples including: individual/skeleton ID, sediment core IDs, extract batch, library batch, sequencing run etc..  These IDs should always act as 'umbrella' IDs that allow association with entries processed together, to allow for downstream analyses of batch effects. Ideally, the information should indicate or specify what type of batch the ID is describing.

samp_category.description: sample category. The type/category of a sample. "Sample" includes biological and technical replicates.

samp_decont_pretreat.description: sample decontamination pretreatment. Protocols employed for sample surface decontamination of external  modern nucleic acids; Treatment used on the samples immediately prior to nucleic acid extraction. Dependant on the sample type.  More relevant for bones than environmental samples. E.g. buffers, EDTA, etc.. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

damage_treatment.description: damage treatment type. Indication of whether characteristic ancient DNA damage has been altered or removed from a DNA extract in a laboratory. If damage has been removed, but whether it was fully or partially removed is unknown (e.g. with UDG treatment) - specify 'other', and describe known information in `sop_experimental` and related free text descriptive terms.

nucl_acid_extr_date.description: date of extraction of nucleic acids from sample. The date when the nucleic acid extraction was started from the sample material. In case no exact time is available, the date can be right truncated i.e. all of these are valid times: 2008-01-23T19:23:10+00:00; 2008-01-23T19:23:10; 2008-01-23; 2008-01; 2008; Except: 2008-01; 2008 all are ISO8601 compliant

sop_experimental.description: experimental standard operating procedure. Provide a DOI or URL to refer to the paper where the field report, nucleic acid extraction,  library construction, and other procedures are explained in more detail, e.g. the paper reporting the data.. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

lib_mid_desc.value: dual index with single internal barcode.
lib_mid_desc.description: description of library multiplex identifiers or indexing configuration. Index/barcode/primer configuration used during library building for sequencing. This includes information such as the number, type and location of indexes, the index/primer kit/list, or if 'inline' barcodes or UMIs were ligated directly onto the template molecules.

library_name.description: library name. Any ID or name used for referring to a nucleic acid sequencing library associated with the sample.

lib_polymerase.description: library polymerase. The polymerase enzyme used for building nucleic acid libraries. Include formal identifier e.g. SKU or the manufacturers name at minimum.

lib_strandedness.description: nucleic acid strandedness in library creation. The strandedness of the original template nucleic acid molecules used for constructing the sequencing library

lib_gener_technique.description: library generation technique. The technique used to generate the library, i.e., amplicon, enriched, or shotgun. An amplicon library is a library that has been amplified to target a single specific region of a genome (e.g. a specific gene). An enriched library is a library that has had a particular genome or multiple genomic regions/positions 'captured' or enriched typically via baits/probes. A shotgun library has undergone no type of targeted amplification/enrichment for a particular genomic region or genome, i.e., random sequencing of any nucleic acid molecule contained in a genomic library.

sop_lib_preparation.description: library preparation protocols. Citation(s) for the nucleic acid library preparation protocol.. Syntax: ^({PMID}|{DOI}|{URL})$

reamp_pcr_cyc_tot.description: number of reamplification cycles. Number of amplification cycles after library indexing PCR. If capture data, this refers to amplifications prior to the capture experiments.

capt_pcr_cyc_tot.description: post capture PCR reamplication cycles total. Amplification cycles after capture enrichment total. Provide additional information about PCR conditions in pcr_cond

capt_probe_src_taxid.description: Genomic capture probe source taxonomy IDs. NCBI taxon ID(s) of all organisms included in the baits of a whole organelle or whole genome-level capture panel. There should be an (ideally) species level taxonomic ID entry for each organism that had sequences included in the design. If whole genera were targeted, you can instead use a single genus level taxonomic ID or that of any relevant higher taxonomic unit.

capt_probe_desc.value: Custom probe design (70 bp biotinylated RNA probes) covering 500 full E. Coli genomes; company TE-Science
capt_probe_desc.description: capture probe design description. Description of target enrichment probe designs used (e.g., species included, sequences, type, company). This can include custom kits (please provide a general description and DOI if available) or commercially available kit (provide ID and company).

data_preproc_desc.value: Adapter trimmed, quality filtered, and host reads removed through mapping for ethical reasons.
data_preproc_desc.description: description of sequencing reads preprocessing. Description of preprocessing performed on the reads in the sequencing data file. Describe any in silico processing or modification of the sequencing reads away from the original state as received from the sequencer. This should include details such as adapter-, barcode-, and/or quality- trimming, or any filtering such as for read length or of off-target reads.

reads_removed.description: description of reads removal. Specify whether associated data was filtered in some form prior to upload, such as host reads removal. Detailed description of the the data filtering that was carried out should be described in term 'preprocessing of sequencing reads description'.
